Below the rule: chapter heading, italic chapter title, then the opening paragraph with a large initial E. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: nosmet jure tuemur: Ubi enim vulnus infligitur, ibi mortis imminet periculum si non proxime, saltem remote, & in potentiâ. Præterquam, quod ex aliis juris textubus manife-ste appareat, etiam ubi proxi-mè mortis periculum non est, aggressorem impune occidi posse.
main_text.head: CAP. XXII.

head.i: Utrum fugere teneatur, qui fugere potuit?

main_text.p: ET si insultatus, periculum quantum in se est evitare teneatur, in tantum etiam, ut si insultantem interimat, modo aliter sibi consulere potuisset, in l. Corneliam de Sicariis incidat. Tamen quia nonnunquam, si non plerumque, qui fugæ se mandat, in periculum incidit, dicendum eum non

page.notes: The chapter heading is set in spaced capitals with stops between the letters; transcribed as "CAP. XXII.". The page number "171" is printed at top right and is slightly smudged, so the last digit is read with some doubt. Ink spots and scan marks were ignored. The catchword "sem-" is at the lower right, below the last line of text.
